mainTopic: A warned, deliberate false deposit oath: מלקות, קרבן, or both, and רבה's rule that denying a debt that has witnesses brings no קרבן
overview: רב כהנא asks about someone who deliberately swears falsely about a deposit (שבועת הפקדון) after witnesses warned him. Does he bring the usual אשם, get only מלקות, or get both? A first proof from a ברייתא is pushed aside in two ways. רבא בר איתי says it follows only רבי שמעון. רב כהנא says the correct wording of the ברייתא never mentions מלקות. Further proofs fall away because they might be about someone who was never warned. A ברייתא comparing a נזיר טמא to a deposit oath is also deflected: 'not flogged' may simply mean that lashes alone do not finish his case. רבה then objects that when witnesses exist, a false denial is only empty words. This shows he holds that denying a debt that has עדים brings no קרבן. רבה himself turns down a ברייתא offered in his support, and the גמרא begins a list of proofs against his rule, starting with a משנה about two sets of witnesses.

steps.title: Warned intentional false deposit oath: lashes, offering, or both?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks what happens when someone intentionally swears falsely about a deposit after witnesses warned him. He lays out three possibilities.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone deliberately swore falsely about a deposit and was warned, what is the law? Maybe, since this whole law is unusual (an intentional sinner bringing a קרבן), it doesn't matter whether he was warned, and he brings the offering either way. Or maybe that only applies when he wasn't warned, but once he was warned he gets מלקות and no קרבן. Or maybe we do both.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks a question that has three possible answers. He wants to know what happens to a deliberate false swearer about a deposit who was formally warned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rules collide here. In the rest of the תורה, a deliberate sinner never brings a קרבן, and a warned sinner gets מלקות. שבועת הפקדון is an exception to the first rule, so the question is whether that exception also overrides the normal מלקות outcome, gives way to it, or sits next to it.

keyTerms.meaning: a false oath denying that one holds someone else's deposit or money
they warned him (התראה), which is needed before מלקות
an unusual law that breaks the normal pattern
we do both this and that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume a deliberate sinner can never bring a קרבן. שבועת הפקדון is exactly the famous case where a מזיד does bring one. The question here is only about the warned case.

phrases.english: to them: If one intentionally swore falsely about a deposit
phrases.notes: This sentence started just before this point. רב כהנא is putting the question to רבה's students.

phrases.english: and they warned him, what is the law?
Since it is a novelty,
for in the entire Torah we do not find
an intentional sinner who brings an offering,
and here he does bring an offering,
there is no difference whether they warned him
and no difference whether they did not warn him?
Or perhaps, this applies
only where they did not warn him;
but where they warned him,
he is flogged, and does not bring an offering;
or perhaps, we do both.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵזִיד בִּשְׁבוּעַת הַפִּקָּדוֹן וְהִתְרוּ בּוֹ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the inquiry
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a warned מזיד in שבועת הפקדון brings an אשם, receives מלקות, or both

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: lashes, not an offering
steps.stepSummary: The students quote a ברייתא saying that intentional שבועת הפקדון gets מלקות. That implies he was warned, and that he gets מלקות but no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: we learned that שבועת הפקדון is stricter than the oath of testimony, because if done on purpose one gets מלקות, and if done by mistake one brings an אשם worth silver shekels. Since it says מלקות for the intentional case, he must have been warned. So it is saying מלקות, yes, but a קרבן, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The students try to settle רב כהנא's question using a ברייתא. They argue it supports the second option: מלקות only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות can only happen if there was a warning, so the ברייתא's intentional case must be a warned case. It assigns the קרבן only to the unintentional case and assigns מלקות to the intentional one. From that split they infer there is no קרבן when he was warned.

keyTerms.meaning: its intentional violation / its unintentional violation

phrases.english: They said to him: We learned:
An oath on a deposit is stricter than it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the oath of testimony (שבועת העדות), the oath being compared here.

phrases.english: for one is liable to lashes for its intentional violation
and for its unintentional violation, a guilt-offering worth silver shekels.
Since it says lashes for its intentional violation,
it follows that they warned him;
and it says: lashes, yes; an offering, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 using a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That a warned מזיד in שבועת הפקדון gets מלקות and no קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'חמורה הימנה שבועת הפקדון שחייבין על זדונה מכות ועל שגגתה אשם'

steps.title: Why lashes count as the stricter result
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why getting מלקות is called a 'stringency' and answers that people would rather bring a קרבן than be flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the stringency? A person would rather bring an offering than be flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain one word in the ברייתא: why it calls the deposit oath 'stricter.' It asks and answers in one line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath of testimony always ends in a קרבן, even when done on purpose. The deposit oath, when done on purpose, ends in מלקות instead. Since people prefer paying for an offering over physical lashes, the deposit oath is the harsher one.

keyTerms.meaning: he prefers, it is easier for him

phrases.english: And what is the stringency?
That a person prefers
to bring an offering and not be flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the word חמורה in the ברייתא cited in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what sense getting מלקות is 'stricter'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People prefer bringing a קרבן over receiving lashes

steps.title: The ברייתא follows only רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר איתי rejects the proof. The ברייתא reflects רבי שמעון's view that an intentional deposit oath gets no atonement, but according to the רבנן he brings a קרבן too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר איתי said to them: Who taught that an intentional false deposit oath does not get atonement? רבי שמעון. But according to the רבנן, he also brings an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר איתי knocks down the students' proof. He shows that the ברייתא follows only one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'no קרבן for the intentional case' matches רבי שמעון, who holds that an intentional deposit oath has no קרבן atonement at all. The רבנן hold that even a מזיד brings an אשם, so under their view he gets מלקות and also brings a קרבן. The ברייתא therefore cannot settle רב כהנא's question for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא who taught this?
was not given atonement (through a קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that gives מלקות and no קרבן follows רבי שמעון. According to the רבנן, a warned מזיד in שבועת הפקדון gets both מלקות and a קרבן, so רב כהנא's question is not proven from it.

phrases.english: Rava bar Itai said to them:
Who taught that an intentional oath on a deposit
was not given atonement?
Rabbi Shimon;
but according to the Rabbis, he also brings an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תָּנָא זְדוֹן שְׁבוּעַת הַפִּקָּדוֹן לֹא נִיתַּן לְכַפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to רבי שמעון's view, so it does not decide the question for the רבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'no קרבן' in the ברייתא comes from רבי שמעון's general view that an intentional deposit oath gets no atonement. It does not come from the warning, so it says nothing about the רבנן's view.

steps.title: רב כהנא says the ברייתא actually reads differently
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rejects the proof from the ברייתא. He teaches it with other wording, and in his wording the stringency of שבועת הפקדון is about the cost of the קרבן, not about מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to them: Leave that ברייתא aside, because I am the one who teaches it, and this is how I teach it: whether he swore falsely on purpose or by mistake, he brings an אשם worth silver shekels. And what is the stringency? With an oath of testimony he brings a חטאת that can cost as little as a דנקא, but here he brings an אשם worth silver shekels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא says the students cannot prove anything from that ברייתא, because the correct wording does not mention מלקות at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students' proof depended on the ברייתא saying that a deliberate false deposit oath gets מלקות. In רב כהנא's wording, the 'stringency' is that the קרבן is expensive: an אשם worth at least two shekels, compared with the cheap חטאת of שבועת העדות. Without any mention of מלקות, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it aside; apart from this
Silver shekels; the אשם must be worth at least two
A sin-offering that can be worth as little as a danka (a sixth of a dinar)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'stringency' is not מלקות. It is that the קרבן for a deposit oath costs much more than the קרבן for an oath of testimony.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to them:
Leave that one aside;
for I am the one who teaches it,
and this is how I teach it:
whether intentional or unintentional,
a guilt-offering worth silver shekels.
And what is the stringency?
That there, a sin-offering worth a danka,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the oath of testimony, whose קרבן can be very cheap.

phrases.english: and here, a guilt-offering worth silver shekels.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר מִינַּהּ דְּהַהִיא; דַּאֲנָא תָּנֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא בר איתי's rejection, רב כהנא gives a second, independent rejection of the proof by correcting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The students quoted the wrong wording. The real ברייתא says nothing about מלקות.

steps.title: Why not answer the question from רב כהנא's own wording?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רב כהנא's own wording says even a deliberate false oath brings a קרבן, so that should settle his question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him learn the answer from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא: his own wording seems to answer his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wording says that even a deliberate (זדון) false deposit oath brings an אשם and mentions no מלקות. That seems to show a deliberate swearer brings a קרבן and is not flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him learn from it

phrases.english: Then let him learn from it!
phrases.notes: From his own wording, which says even someone who swore falsely on purpose brings a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב כהנא's corrected wording into a possible answer to his own question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's question still being open
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His wording says זדון brings an אשם with no מלקות, so the question looks answered.

steps.title: Maybe the case is one with no warning
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רב כהנא's wording may be talking about someone who was not warned, and that case is not what he asked about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is talking about a case where they did not warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why his wording does not answer his question: it may be about a person who was never warned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without התראה, there can be no מלקות, so of course he brings a קרבן. רב כהנא asked about someone who was warned, where מלקות is possible. So the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him (התראה), which is needed for מלקות

phrases.english: Perhaps they did not warn him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the wording to an unwarned person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His wording covers every deliberate swearer, warned or not.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may only cover someone who was not warned, so it says nothing about the warned case he asked about.

steps.title: Another version: a proof from a source saying intentional brings an אשם
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the discussion, the גמרא tries to prove from a source that a deliberate false deposit oath brings an אשם, even when he was warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: Come and hear: One is not liable for doing it by mistake. What is one liable for doing it on purpose? An אשם worth silver shekels. Isn't this talking about a case where they warned him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells the discussion another way. This time it tries to answer רב כהנא from a source that says the deliberate swearer brings an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source names only an אשם for the deliberate case. If that case includes a warned person, then a warned person brings a קרבן and is not flogged, which answers the question.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? (pushing for a proof)

phrases.english: Another version: Come and hear:
One is not liable for doing it by mistake.
What is one liable for doing it on purpose?
A guilt-offering worth silver shekels.
What, is it not where they warned him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion, where a proof is brought from the משנה's wording that a זדון case brings an אשם.
steps.raayaObject: A warned, deliberate false deposit oath brings an אשם and not מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source that says the deliberate case brings an אשם worth silver shekels.

steps.title: Again, maybe he was not warned
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected the same way: the source may be talking about someone who was not warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a case where they did not warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the proof away by saying the source is about an unwarned person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same move as in step 7. Without a warning there is no מלקות, so an אשם is expected, and the warned case remains unresolved.

phrases.english: Here too, where they did not warn him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second-version proof by limiting it to an unwarned case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the source is talking about a warned person, but it could be about an unwarned one.

steps.title: Proof from comparing an impure nazir to a deposit oath
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא contrasts a נזיר טמא, who is flogged, with someone who swore falsely about a deposit, who is not. Since flogging requires a warning, both cases involve a warned person, so the warned deposit-swearer is not flogged but brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: No. If you said so about an impure נזיר, who is flogged, will you say so about a deposit oath, where he is not flogged? Since it says the נזיר is flogged, he must have been warned. And it says the deposit-swearer is not flogged, which means he does bring a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to answer רב כהנא. From its wording it shows that a warned person who swears falsely about a deposit brings a קרבן and gets no מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר is said to be flogged, which is only possible with התראה, so the ברייתא is talking about warned people. In that same warned setting, it says the deposit-swearer is not flogged. That implies he brings a קרבן instead. This time the 'maybe he wasn't warned' answer does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the ברייתא speaks about a warned person, it finally addresses the exact case רב כהנא asked about.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
No; if you said so about an impure nazirite,
who is indeed flogged,
will you say so about an oath on a deposit,
where he is not flogged?!
Since it says he is flogged,
it follows that they warned him;

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר תֹּאמַר בִּשְׁבוּעַת הַפִּקָּדוֹן שֶׁאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה –
phrases.english: and it says, 'will you say so about an oath on a deposit, where he is not flogged?'
but he does bring an offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier proofs failed because they might be about someone who was not warned. This proof comes from a ברייתא that is clearly about a warned person.
steps.raayaObject: A warned, deliberate false deposit oath brings a קרבן and gets no מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting נזיר טמא (flogged, so warned) with שבועת הפקדון (not flogged).

steps.title: Not flogged means not settled by lashes alone
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the ברייתא is turned down by reading 'אינו לוקה' differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he is not flogged' mean? It means his case is not finished off with lashes alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 10 by giving the words 'he is not flogged' a new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 read 'not flogged' to mean that a warned deposit-swearer gets no lashes and brings a קרבן instead. Now the גמרא says the phrase only means lashes are not enough to end his case, because he also needs a קרבן. On this reading he may get both lashes and a קרבן, so the ברייתא does not prove the 'קרבן without lashes' option.

keyTerms.meaning: is exempted, finished with his obligation

phrases.english: What does 'he is not flogged' mean?
phrases.notes: These are the words of the ברייתא from step 10, about the person who swore falsely about a deposit.

phrases.english: That he is not exempted through lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a warned deposit-swearer brings a קרבן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Not flogged' can mean 'lashes alone do not end his case.' So even when warned he may get both lashes and a קרבן, rather than a קרבן in place of lashes.

steps.title: But the impure נזיר also brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: If the deposit-swearer is not settled by lashes, then the contrast implies the נזיר טמא is settled by lashes. Yet the תורה gives him a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean an impure נזיר is finished off with lashes? But the תורה writes that he brings a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts the two cases. If the deposit-swearer 'is not finished with lashes,' then the נזיר טמא must be someone who is finished with lashes. That cannot be right, because the תורה clearly gives the נזיר טמא a קרבן.

phrases.english: By implication, an impure nazirite is exempted through lashes?!
But 'offering' is written about him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אינו לוקה' means 'not exempted through lashes.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contrast would mean the נזיר טמא is exempted by lashes, but a פסוק gives him a קרבן.

steps.title: The נזיר's offering is to restart his נזירות in purity
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר טמא's קרבן does not atone for his sin. It lets his נזירות start again while he is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he brings a קרבן so that his נזירות can take effect on him in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר טמא's קרבן is not a כפרה for doing wrong. It is a technical step that lets him begin his נזירות again in טהרה. So for the sin itself, lashes really are the only consequence, and the reading from step 11 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the state of being a נזיר

phrases.english: There, the reason he brings an offering
is so that there will take effect on him
a naziriteship in purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם דְּמַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתֵיחוּל עֲלֵיהּ נְזִירוּת בְּטׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נזיר טמא's קרבן atones for his sin, so lashes are not his only consequence.
steps.terutzMaskana: His קרבן only lets him restart his נזירות in purity. For the sin itself, lashes are the whole story.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ברייתא is gone. 'Not flogged' can mean 'needs a קרבן, not just lashes,' and the נזיר's קרבן is only for purification.

steps.title: רבה asks: with witnesses, the denial is just empty words
steps.stepSummary: רבה hears רב כהנא's question and objects to its hidden assumption. That assumption is that an unwarned person who swore falsely, when there are witnesses, brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים told this to רבה. He said: Does it follow that if they did not warn him and there are witnesses, he is liable? It is just a denial in words!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks something that רב כהנא's question took for granted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A warning is given by witnesses, so רב כהנא's case has עדים. The answers 'perhaps he was not warned' (steps 7 and 9) assume that a person with עדים but no warning brings a קרבן. רבה objects: if witnesses can prove the debt, the false denial costs the owner nothing. It is just empty words, so why should it bring a קרבן?

keyTerms.meaning: a denial in words only, with no real effect

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rabba.
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב כהנא's question about a warned person who swore falsely on purpose.

phrases.english: He said to them:
By implication, when they did not warn him
and there are witnesses, he is liable?!
It is merely a denial in words!
phrases.notes: Since witnesses can prove the debt, his lie can't actually make the owner lose the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּכִי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ וְאִיכָּא עֵדִים מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the warning question to a new problem: what happens when witnesses exist.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in רב כהנא's question that an unwarned false swearer brings a קרבן even when there are עדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When witnesses exist, the denial causes no real loss, so it should not count as a denial that brings a קרבן.

steps.title: רבה holds that denying money that has witnesses is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out רבה's general rule from his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: So רבה holds: one who denies money that has witnesses is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the rule that sits behind רבה's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's challenge only works if a false denial against witnesses counts for nothing. So the גמרא states his position plainly: a כופר in a money case that has עדים is פטור from the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: one who denies a money claim

phrases.english: Evidently Rabba holds:

phrases.aramaic: הַכּוֹפֵר בְּמָמוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: One who denies money that has witnesses is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the rule that step 14 depends on.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבה, a false oath denying a debt that witnesses can prove does not bring a קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the passage, where people try to prove or disprove רבה's rule.

steps.title: רב חנינא brings a ברייתא to support רבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'ונשבע על שקר' that a borrower with a שטר or with עדים is excluded. That seems to back רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא said to רבה: A ברייתא supports you. 'And he denies it' leaves out one who admits to one of the brothers or one of the partners. 'And swears falsely' leaves out one who borrowed with a document or with witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא offers a source that seems to prove רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a borrower whose loan has a שטר or עדים is excluded from the false-oath קרבן. That looks exactly like רבה's view that denying a debt with witnesses brings no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: one who borrowed with a written document

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina said to Rabba,
A baraita is taught that supports you:
'And he deals falsely therein'
excludes one who admits to one of the brothers
or to one of the partners.
'And swears to a lie'
excludes one who borrows with a document and one who borrows with witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the rule in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's rule that denying money with witnesses is פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 5:22 that excludes a borrower with a שטר or with עדים.

steps.title: רבה: the ברייתא is about someone who admits the loan
steps.stepSummary: רבה turns down the support. The ברייתא's borrower admits he borrowed and only denies the witnesses or the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: If you mean this, you have not supported me. The ברייתא is about one who says, 'I borrowed, but not in front of witnesses,' or 'I borrowed, but not with a document.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה himself rejects the proof that was offered in his favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the borrower does not deny the debt at all. He only lies about how the loan was made, so of course there is no קרבן. That says nothing about a person who denies the whole debt when witnesses exist, so the ברייתא cannot prove רבה's rule.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not taking back his opinion. He only says this particular ברייתא doesn't prove it.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is because of this,
you have not supported us;
it is where he says, 'I borrowed, but I did not borrow in front of witnesses,'
or 'I borrowed, but I did not borrow with a document.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support offered in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of the ברייתא as a proof for רבה's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא speaks of someone who admits the debt and only denies how it was made, not someone who denies the debt itself.

steps.title: רבה points to the brothers case to back his reading
steps.stepSummary: רבה shows where in the ברייתא we see that it is talking about a denial of words only. He points to its case of admitting to one of the brothers or partners.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see this? From what the ברייתא teaches: 'and deals falsely therein' excludes one who admits to one of the brothers or to one of the partners.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is backing up his claim from Step 17 by pointing to another part of the same ברייתא. This sets up the next lines, which will explain that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, רבה said the ברייתא's borrower only denies the עדים or the שטר, not the loan itself. Now he points to the brothers case in the same ברייתא. He will use it to show that the whole ברייתא is about denials of details.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And deals falsely therein,' from the פסוק of שבועת הפקדון

phrases.english: From where?
phrases.notes: He means: where in the ברייתא do we see that it is talking about a denial of details only?

phrases.english: From that it teaches: 'and deals falsely therein'
excludes one who admits to one of the brothers
or to one of the partners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the evidence for רבה's rejection in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that the ברייתא's last clause is about a כפירת דברים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The brothers/partners clause of the same ברייתא

steps.title: What is the brothers case? Not admitting only one brother's half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the brothers case looks like. It rejects the idea that he admitted only one brother's half, because then he would be denying the other brother's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case of 'to one of the brothers,' what are its circumstances? If we say he admitted to one brother his own half, there is still the denial of the other brother!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks how to picture the brothers case and rules out the first, simple option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he admitted only to one brother's half, he would be denying the other half, which is real money. A denial of real money should make him liable. So the ברייתא, which exempts him, must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? (How do we picture the case?)

phrases.english: This case of 'to one of the brothers'
what are its circumstances?
If we say that he admitted to him
his own half,
but there is the denial of the other one!
phrases.notes: He would still be denying the other brother's real money, so he should not be exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי לְאֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the clause that רבה pointed to in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact case is 'admits to one of the brothers'?

steps.title: He admits the whole debt but says he borrowed from only one brother
steps.stepSummary: The brothers say he borrowed from both of them. He answers that he borrowed the whole sum from one of them. He admits all the money, so he only denies a detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that they said to him, 'You borrowed from both of us,' and he said to them, 'No, I borrowed from one of you,' which is only a denial of words?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the correct picture of the brothers case: the borrower admits the full amount and only argues about whom he borrowed it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he admits owing all the money, he is not denying any money. He only denies a detail of the loan, which is called a כפירת דברים. That is why the ברייתא exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely a denial of words (details), not of money

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that they said to him:
'You borrowed from both of us';
and he said to them: 'No,
I borrowed from one of you'
which is merely a denial of words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19's question after ruling out the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The brothers case is one where he admits the whole debt and denies only that he borrowed from both brothers, a כפירת דברים.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא is about denying details only
steps.stepSummary: Since the first clause is a denial of words, the last clause about the שטר and עדים is also a denial of words. So the ברייתא does not prove רבה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the first clause is a denial of words, the last clause is also a denial of words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה wraps up his rejection of the ברייתא as proof for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's clauses go together. The brothers clause is about denying a detail, so the clause about the borrower with a שטר or עדים is too. He admits the loan and only denies the document or witnesses. That is why he is exempt, not because עדים exist.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of 'וכחש בה' exempts someone who admits the money and only denies a detail. It says nothing about someone who denies the money when there are עדים, so it cannot prove רבה's rule.

phrases.english: And since the first clause is a denial of words,
the last clause is also a denial of words.
phrases.notes: The last clause is the borrower with a שטר or with עדים from Step 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרֵישָׁא כְּפִירַת דְּבָרִים סֵיפָא נָמֵי כְּפִירַת דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the brothers case from Step 20 to the clause in question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's exemption is about a כפירת דברים, so it gives no support to רבה.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה that an intentional false oath brings an אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid for the coming proofs. It then brings a משנה: for an intentional false oath he brings an אשם worth two silver shekels. Maybe this means intentional even when there are עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: liability; sets; of the homeowner; stringent; nazirite.) Come hear: He is not liable for the oath when it is unwitting. And what is he liable for when it is intentional? An אשם worth silver shekels. Isn't this intentional when there are עדים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a series of proofs that someone who swears falsely is liable even when there are עדים, against רבה. This is the first proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an intentional false oath about a deposit brings an אשם. The גמרא suggests this means he knew there were עדים against him and swore anyway. If so, there is a קרבן even with עדים, which goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists the coming proofs
Silver shekels (the אשם must be worth at least two)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'זדון' here. 'זדון עדים' means he swore falsely while עדים exist. 'זדון עצמו' means only he knows; there are no עדים.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: liability; sets;
of the homeowner; stringent; nazirite)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַל שִׁגְגָתָהּ.
phrases.english: Come hear: He is not liable for its unwitting oath.
And what is he liable for its intentional oath?
A guilt-offering worth silver shekels.
What, is it not intentional when there are witnesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַל שִׁגְגָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה, the גמרא turns to proofs against his rule.
steps.raayaObject: That a false oath is liable for a קרבן even when there are עדים, against רבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that an intentional false oath brings an אשם worth silver shekels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'intentional' means swearing falsely while עדים exist, the משנה gives a קרבן even with עדים.

steps.title: No: the משנה means he admits on his own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. 'Intentional' means he himself admits he knew, with no עדים involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means intentional by his own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 22 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה can be about a case with no עדים, where he himself confesses he swore falsely on purpose. Then the משנה does not tell us about a case with עדים, and רבה's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Swearing falsely when there are witnesses
Intentional by his own admission, with no witnesses

phrases.english: No, intentional by himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'intentional' means with עדים, but it can mean his own admission with no עדים.

steps.title: Proof from two sets of witnesses who both denied
steps.stepSummary: A second proof: two sets of עדים both falsely deny knowing the testimony. Both sets are liable, because the testimony could stand with either set.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: If there were two sets of witnesses, and the first denied and afterward the second denied, both are liable, because the testimony can stand with either of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof against רבה, from the laws of שבועת העדות. The point of the proof will become clear in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first set denied while a second set of עדים still existed, much like swearing falsely when there are עדים. Yet the משנה says the first set is liable too. This may show that a false oath is liable even when other עדים exist.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּתֵּי עֵדִים,
phrases.english: Come hear: There were two sets of witnesses,
the first set denied
and afterward the second set denied,
both are liable,
because the testimony can stand with either of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּתֵּי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof after the first one was rejected in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That a false oath is liable even when other עדים exist, against רבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two sets of עדים in שבועת העדות

steps.title: Why is the first set liable if the second set was still there?
steps.stepSummary: The second set's liability makes sense, because the first set had already denied. But the first set should seem exempt, since the second set could still testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the second set should be liable, since the first set already denied. But why is the first set liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the משנה in order to bring out the proof. This sets up the explanation that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the second set denied, they were the only עדים left, so their denial really caused a loss. When the first set denied, the second set was still available. So the first set's false oath did not seem to cause any loss. The answer to this question is where the proof against רבה will come from.

phrases.english: Granted, the second set should be liable,
since the first set already denied;
but the first set, why is it liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the משנה from Step 24 to set up the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the first set liable, when other עדים were still available to testify?
